text.en: India is rich in biodiversity, and it is home to elephants, tigers and leopards. About three-fourths of the world’s tigers and about three-fifths of the Asiatic elephants live in India. In this chapter you will add and subtract big numbers to count these animals, and you will learn clever shortcuts to solve sums quickly.

Let us play the NIM game for two players, where each player adds either 1 or 2 to the running total. The player who reaches 10 first is the winner. If the other player has reached 8 and it is your turn, add 2 and you reach 10, so you win. If the other player has reached 7 and it is your turn, you lose, because adding 1 gives 8 and adding 2 gives 9, and the other player reaches 10. If the other player has reached 6, you add 1 to make 7, and then you can always win. So 7, 4 and 1 are the safe numbers: if you reach one of them, you can always win the game.
The addition chart has numbers 0 to 12 on the top and on the side, and each cell is the row number plus the column number. The numbers in a row go up by 1 as we move right, and the numbers in a column go up by 1 as we move down. The number 9 appears 10 times in the chart, and a number like 12 appears many times because many pairs add up to it. No row or column has only even numbers or only odd numbers, because even and odd numbers alternate. In a 2 by 2 window, the two diagonal sums are always equal, which is a lovely pattern.
Take 27 and reverse it to get 72, and 27 + 72 = 99. Adding a 2-digit number and its reverse always gives a multiple of 11, because the tens and ones digits are both added. Numbers that give 55 when added to their reverse are 14, 23, 32 and 41, and numbers that give 88 are 17, 26, 35, 44, 53, 62 and 71. The smallest 3-digit sum is 110, for example 19 + 91 = 110.
The elephants in Karnataka number 6049 and in Kerala 3054, so we add 6049 + 3054. First estimate: 6000 + 3000 is about 9000. Ones: 9 + 4 = 13, so write 3 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, so write 0 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Thousands: 6 + 3 = 9, so there are 9103 elephants in the two states, which is close to our estimate. Remember that 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred and 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.
Gujarat has 1355 leopards, Karnataka has 1131 and Madhya Pradesh has 1817. The estimate is 1000 + 1000 + 2000, about 4000. Ones: 5 + 1 + 7 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 1 + 8 + 1 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 thousand. Thousands: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4, so there are 4303 leopards in the three states.
Maharashtra has 444 tigers, and Madhya Pradesh has 341 more, so 444 + 341 = 785 tigers. Uttarakhand has 116 more than Maharashtra, so 444 + 116 = 560 tigers. Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand together have 785 + 560 = 1345 tigers. All three states have 444 + 1345 = 1789 tigers. When a problem says more than, we add, and when it says less than, we subtract.
Assam has 5719 elephants, which is 3965 more than Meghalaya, so Meghalaya has 5719 − 3965. The estimate is 5700 − 4000, about 1700. Ones: 9 − 5 = 4. Tens: 1 is less than 6, so regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens, which makes 11 tens, and 11 − 6 = 5. Hundreds: 6 is left and 9 is more than 6, so regroup 1 thousand as 10 hundreds, which makes 16 hundreds, and 16 − 9 = 7. Thousands: 4 is left and 4 − 3 = 1, so Meghalaya has 1754 elephants. To find an earlier number after an increase, subtract: leopards in 2018 were 8820 − 749 = 8071.
To add 99, add 100 and then subtract 1, so 4596 + 104 is 4600 + 100 = 4700. To subtract 99, subtract 100 and then add 1, so 8787 − 99 = 8688. When two numbers are close to round numbers, we can use the round number and then adjust. To compare 54 + 97 and 54 + 90, notice that the same 54 is added, so the bigger number added gives the bigger total. Without calculating, 84 − 68 is more than 90 − 68? No, the same 68 is taken away from a smaller 84, so 84 − 68 is less than 90 − 68. Always estimate first, then check whether your answer is close.

problem.en: Karnataka has 6049 elephants and Kerala has 3054. How many in all?

why.en: The word in all tells us to add.

text.en: Ones: 9 + 4 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 ten.
Tens: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1.
Thousands: 6 + 3 = 9, so the answer is 9103.

problem.en: Assam has 5719 elephants, which is 3965 more than Meghalaya. How many does Meghalaya have?

text.en: Meghalaya has fewer, so we subtract 5719 − 3965.

why.en: More than means the other number is smaller.

text.en: Ones 9 − 5 = 4. Tens: regroup, 11 − 6 = 5.
Hundreds: regroup, 16 − 9 = 7. Thousands: 4 − 3 = 1.
Meghalaya has 1754 elephants.

problem.en: In Kaziranga, 6415 visitors came in November, which is 1587 more than October. How many came in October?

text.en: We subtract, so 6415 − 1587.
Ones: 15 − 7 = 8. Tens: 0 − 8 needs regrouping, 10 − 8 = 2.

why.en: Borrow from the hundreds and the tens.

text.en: Hundreds: 3 − 5 needs regrouping, 13 − 5 = 8. Thousands: 5 − 1 = 4.
October had 4828 visitors.
Notice that 4596 is close to 4600, because 4596 + 4 = 4600.
Take 4 from 104 to give to 4596, so 4600 + 100.

prompt.en: Explain how you add and subtract 4-digit numbers, and how estimating and easy ways help.

requiredIdeas.en: Write numbers in columns with ones under ones
Start from the ones and regroup when 10 or more
Subtract from the ones and borrow when the top digit is smaller
Estimate first to check the answer
Use round numbers to make quick adjustments

commonMisconceptions.en: Forgetting to add the carried digit
Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger
Not checking if the answer is close to the estimate

points.en: We add big numbers column by column from the ones, carrying when a column makes 10 or more.
We subtract column by column, borrowing from the next place when needed.
More than means add and less than means subtract.
Estimating first helps us check our answer.
Easy ways: add or subtract 100 and adjust, or use round numbers.
Adding a number to its reverse gives a multiple of 11.
